construction.isolation_detail: Prior global observer incorrectly included obj:P3-bears. After actor scoping and native COMBAT_DECLARE_BLOCKERS phase scoping, obj:P3-bears is absent while obj:P2-bears remains. The remaining discrepancy is therefore not observer actor/phase scope.

terminal_postconditions: P2 blocker options contain only attackers for which P2 is defending player.

frozen_obligation_authority.manifest_expected_observation: P2 legal blockers never include blockers controlled by P3 or P4 and never include attackers outside P2 defending scope.
required_assertions: for each P2 blocker b, blocker_controller(b) == P2
if b blocks attacker a, defender_of(a) == P2
frozen_obligation_authority.ws44_repair_detail: Dangling blocker semantic ID obj:mp-blocker was repaired to obj:mp-p2-blocker.
frozen_obligation_authority.finding: The frozen obligation requires defender/blocker partition but does not require obj:mp-p2-blocker to be the only otherwise-legal P2 blocker.

current_rules_authority.source: Wizards of the Coast Magic Comprehensive Rules

relevant_rules.302.6: Summoning sickness limits attacking and activated abilities with tap/untap symbols; it does not prohibit blocking.
relevant_rules.509.1a: A defending player chooses untapped creatures they control to block, subject to restrictions and requirements.
relevant_rules.509.1b: Blocking restrictions are effects saying a creature cannot block or cannot block unless a condition is met.
relevant_rules.802.4a: In attack-multiple-players combat, a defending player can block only with creatures they control and only creatures attacking that defender/protected objects.
relevant_rules.802.4b: When determining that defender's legal blocks, attackers of other players and blockers controlled by other players are ignored.

current_rules_authority.adjudication: An untapped vanilla Grizzly Bears controlled by P2 has no rule-based reason to be excluded from P2's blocker legal-option surface in this state.

provider_authority.observer_scope: P2 priority/defending actor during native PhaseType.COMBAT_DECLARE_BLOCKERS
provider_authority.finding: Forge Rules Core independently exposes obj:P2-bears and obj:mp-p2-blocker as legal P2 blockers. Filtering obj:P2-bears solely to match the immutable requested singleton would move legality into the qualification/provider layer and violate the WS45 Rules-Core/no-request-echo boundary.

terminal_adjudication.reason: WS44 v1.0.4 freezes eligible_blockers as a singleton even though its inherited obligation is only defender/blocker partition and current Magic rules plus the exact Forge Rules Core independently make obj:P2-bears legal. Removing the legal P2 blocker in provider/observer code would be request-derived legality or fabricated legal options, explicitly prohibited by the workstream contract. WS45 is forbidden from editing WS44.

next_action: Terminate WS45 fail-closed with a self-contained handoff. A separate contract-authority/coordinator workstream must supersede WS44 with a new immutable provider-neutral materialization that repairs WS05-MP-BLOCK-4 without weakening its frozen defender/blocker-partition obligation, then Forge successor qualification must restart fresh against that successor version with zero imported runtime credit.
